observation_summary: The StrBuilder.contains(char) and indexOf(char) methods were incorrectly iterating over the entire underlying buffer length instead of the actual size of the string builder, leading to false positives when searching for characters that existed in the buffer but were logically removed.
hypothesis: The methods were using 'thisBuf.length' (the capacity of the internal array) as the loop termination condition instead of 'this.size' (the actual number of characters stored in the builder).
prediction: Changing the loop termination condition from 'thisBuf.length' to 'this.size' will correctly restrict the search to the valid portion of the buffer.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows a direct replacement of the loop boundary condition in two methods. This is a classic algorithmic error where the iteration strategy was incorrect because it used the wrong data structure property (capacity vs. size).
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic error in the loop termination logic. The methods were iterating over the entire allocated buffer rather than the active data size. This is a procedural logic error within the methods themselves, fitting the Algorithm/Method definition perfectly. It is not a missing check (Checking) because the logic was present but incorrect, nor is it an initialization error (Assignment/Initialization) because the variables were initialized correctly, just used in the wrong loop condition.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a condition, it is not a guard or validation check; it is the loop termination condition that defines the algorithm's scope.
The issue is not about the initial value of a variable, but the logic of the iteration boundary.
